neighbours.label: Reaching the innermost point: fires on the word that sets up 'core' or 'very' in idioms of depth ('rotten to the core', 'to its core', 'our very soul'); quiet on the same evaluations without the depth idiom.
fire: Investigators found that the whole department was corrupt to the core.
The news of his death shook the small town to its core.
The film is American to the core, loud and proud and full of hope.
Her poems reach into our very souls and stay there for years.
That betrayal chilled the old general to the core.
He was a soldier to the core, even long after he retired.
The election result shook the party to its very foundations.
The song speaks to the very heart of what it means to grieve.
quiet: Investigators found that the whole department was corrupt and badly managed.
The news of his death saddened the small town for weeks.
The film is American in style, loud and proud and full of hope.
Her poems are read in many schools and stay popular for years.
That betrayal angered the old general more than any defeat.
He was a soldier for twenty years, and then he retired.
The election result surprised the party and its supporters.
The song describes what it means to grieve after a loss.

predictions: median fire ~0.45 (probes: 'rotten to' 0.70, 'burrowing to' 0.51, 'our very life' 0.41, 'to its core' 0.35, 'to the very edge' 0.19); near misses < 0.1 ('badly run' 0.05, 'our daily life' 0.014). A physical 'bored down into' leaked 0.45, so near misses avoid digging verbs.
notes: Card: peaks on ' to', ' the', ' very', ' into' before core/depth words; the - pole promotes ' core', ' beneath', ' deepest'.
